name: dotnet-conventions
description: Always-on .NET/C# conventions covering DI registration traps, codegen/scaffold drift discipline, EF Core persist-refetch value handling, loose-mock test-double gaps, NuGet/dependency pin discipline, marker-interface avoidance, XML-doc selectivity, Windows/.NET tooling gotchas (locked build output, MAX_PATH, DefaultAzureCredential cold-start), and HTTP-client resilience-policy scoping.

source.title: .NET Conventions Baseline
source.relationship: Mirrored from the work toolkit's dotnet-conventions pack — the DI-registration and codegen-drift facts are .NET-technical, not employer-specific, so this personal copy applies to any .NET work outside work. Principles 25-35 backfilled 2026-09-08 via the baseline-gap-review skill's occurrence #3 pass — the work toolkit had added these 2026-09-01 (reliability-hardening and entity-cache performance work on a payments service) without a corresponding mirror-back note, an unmanaged drift caught by this pass's baseline-diff step rather than by anything in _Improvements itself. Principle 36 added 2026-09-08 from a Polly-resilience-scoping investigation on a trade-in service, mirrored the same day into the work toolkit.
